title: The Default Bridge Network 🌉
description: Explore how Docker connects containers out‑of‑the‑box and its limitations.

slides.title: The `bridge` Network (Default) 🏗️
slides.content:
# What You Get for Free

When Docker starts, it creates a network called `bridge` (driver: `bridge`). All new containers attach to this network unless told otherwise.

- Subnet: typically `172.17.0.0/16` (can be changed in daemon config).
- Gateway: `172.17.0.1` (the host’s side of the bridge).
- IPs are assigned dynamically from the subnet.

Containers on the default bridge can communicate with each other via IP address, but **not by container name**.

slides.title: Experiment: Two Containers on Default Bridge 🧪
slides.content: Start two containers and try to ping each other by IP:
slides.codeSnippet:
# Start two detached containers
docker run -d --name con1 alpine sleep 3600
docker run -d --name con2 alpine sleep 3600

# Get their IPs
docker inspect -f '{{.NetworkSettings.IPAddress}}' con1
docker inspect -f '{{.NetworkSettings.IPAddress}}' con2

# Ping con2 from con1 using IP
docker exec con1 ping -c 2 172.17.0.3   # use con2's IP

# Try ping by name (should fail)
docker exec con1 ping -c 2 con2

quizData.question: On the default bridge network, containers can resolve each other by their container names.
quizData.explanation: The default bridge does not provide automatic DNS resolution. You must use IP addresses. Custom bridge networks do provide DNS.

slides.title: Limitations of the Default Bridge ⚠️
slides.content:
# Why You Should Move Beyond It

- **No DNS** – must use IP addresses, which change on container restart.
- **No network isolation** – all containers on the default bridge can see each other.
- **No custom subnet or gateway** – you’re stuck with Docker’s defaults.
- **Less secure** – unintended communication is possible.

In production, always create **custom bridge networks** for each application stack.

slides.title: Pro Tip 💡
slides.content:
## Upgrade to Custom Bridges
Even for two containers talking to each other, using a custom network gives you DNS and better control. It’s a single command: `docker network create`.
